title: MATH 12-03 Mastery Challenge: Determinants, Minors, Cofactors, Adjugate, Matrix Inversion & Invariant Laws

questions.promptText: Find the determinant of the $2 \times 2$ matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 4 \\ 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$.
If $A$ is a $3 \times 3$ matrix with $\det(A) = 5$, what is $\det(2A)$?
questions.explanation:
$\det(kA) = k^n \det(A) = 2^3 \times 5 = 8 \times 5 = 40$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $8 \times 5 = 40$.

questions.promptText: What is the Cofactor $C_{23}$ of an element $a_{23}$ in a $3 \times 3$ matrix?
Find the inverse of the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.
questions.explanation:
$\det(A) = (5)(1) - (2)(2) = 5 - 4 = 1$. Swapping diagonal entries and negating off-diagonals: $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{1}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ -2 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $[1, -2; -2, 5]$.

questions.promptText: What happens to the determinant of a matrix if any two of its rows are interchanged?
questions.choiceA: The determinant changes its algebraic sign (multiplied by $-1$)
questions.explanation: A fundamental theorem of determinants states that interchanging any two rows or columns negates the determinant: $\det(A') = -\det(A)$.

questions.promptText: If $\det(A) = 8$ and $\det(B) = -3$, what is $\det(AB)$?
questions.explanation:
By the multiplicative property of determinants: $\det(AB) = \det(A) \det(B) = 8 \times (-3) = -24$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $8 \times (-3) = -24$.

questions.promptText: Evaluate the determinant of the upper triangular matrix $T = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 7 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & -5 \end{bmatrix}$.
questions.explanation:
The determinant of any triangular (or diagonal) matrix is simply the product of its main diagonal elements: $\det(T) = 4 \times 3 \times (-5) = -60$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $4 \times 3 \times (-5) = -60$.

questions.promptText: What is the condition for a square matrix $A$ to be singular (non-invertible)?
questions.explanation: A matrix is singular (has no inverse) if and only if its determinant is zero ($\det(A) = 0$).

questions.promptText: Find the determinant of the $3 \times 3$ matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 \\ 4 & 2 & 6 \end{bmatrix}$.
If $A$ is a non-singular square matrix with $\det(A) = -4$, what is $\det(A^{-1})$?
For what value of $x$ is the matrix $M = \begin{bmatrix} x & 6 \\ 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ singular?
questions.explanation:
For singularity: $\det(M) = 0 \implies 3x - (6)(2) = 0 \implies 3x = 12 \implies x = 4$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $x = 12/3 = 4$.

questions.promptText: What is the relationship between the determinant of a matrix and the determinant of its transpose $\det(A^T)$?
questions.explanation: Transposition does not alter the value of the determinant: $\det(A^T) = \det(A)$.

questions.promptText: Find the cofactor $C_{32}$ in the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 \\ 4 & 2 & 6 \end{bmatrix}$.
questions.explanation:
Minor $M_{32} = \det\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix} = 1(4) - 0(2) = 4$. Cofactor $C_{32} = (-1)^{3+2} M_{32} = -4$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $(-1)^5 (4) = -4$.

questions.promptText: If $A$ is an $n \times n$ matrix, what is $A \cdot \text{adj}(A)$ identically equal to?
questions.explanation: By the fundamental theorem of adjugates: $A \cdot \text{adj}(A) = \text{adj}(A) \cdot A = \det(A) I_n$.

questions.promptText: Evaluate the determinant: $\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 4 & 7 \\ 2 & 5 & 8 \\ 3 & 6 & 9 \end{vmatrix}$.
questions.explanation:
Column 2 - Column 1 = $[3, 3, 3]^T$, and Column 3 - Column 2 = $[3, 3, 3]^T$. Since the columns are linearly dependent, the determinant is 0.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: AP rows/columns $\implies \det = 0$.

questions.promptText: Find the inverse of the diagonal matrix $D = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 \end{bmatrix}$.
questions.explanation:
The inverse of any diagonal matrix is obtained by replacing each diagonal entry $d_{ii}$ with its reciprocal $1/d_{ii}$: $[1/2, 1/5, -1/4] = [0.5, 0.2, -0.25]$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: Diagonal reciprocals $\implies [0.5, 0.2, -0.25]$.

questions.promptText: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$, what is $\det(A B)$?
What is Cramer's Rule used for in linear algebra?
questions.choiceA: Solving a system of linear algebraic equations using determinants: $x_i = \Delta_i / \Delta$
questions.explanation: Gabriel Cramer's rule (1750) provides an explicit determinant ratio solution for non-singular linear systems.

questions.promptText: Find the determinant of the $2 \times 2$ matrix $K = \begin{bmatrix} \cos\theta & -\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta & \cos\theta \end{bmatrix}$.
questions.explanation:
$\det(K) = (\cos\theta)(\cos\theta) - (-\sin\theta)(\sin\theta) = \cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1$.

questions.promptText: If $A$ is a $3 \times 3$ matrix with $\det(A) = 4$, what is $\det(\text{adj}(A))$?
questions.explanation:
For any $n \times n$ matrix, $\det(\text{adj}(A)) = (\det(A))^{n-1}$. For $n = 3$: $4^{3-1} = 4^2 = 16$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $4^2 = 16$.

questions.promptText: Evaluate the determinant: $\begin{vmatrix} 5 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 & 6 \end{vmatrix}$.
questions.explanation:
Lower triangular matrix determinant is the product of main diagonal entries: $5 \times 2 \times 6 = 60$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $5 \times 2 \times 6 = 60$.
